job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

response.passage: Many people believe that the best way to spot birds is to walk quickly through the forest, hoping to surprise them. However, my mentor, Mr. Sharma, taught me that patience is the real secret. Last Sunday, on October 12th, we visited the Okhla Bird Sanctuary to test this. We arrived at 6:00 AM, just as the sun began to rise. Mr. Sharma explained that birds often hide when they hear heavy footsteps, so we must move slowly to avoid scaring them away. Because we walked with extreme caution, we were able to observe a rare Kingfisher for nearly ten minutes. My friend Rohan, who had rushed ahead to the lake, saw nothing but empty branches. The quiet approach allowed us to see the vibrant blue feathers of the bird clearly. By the time we left at 9:00 AM, I realized that moving slowly is the only way to truly enjoy nature. It is not about how much ground you cover, but how carefully you observe the life around you. If you are loud, the birds will simply vanish into the canopy, leaving you with nothing to see.
response.summary: The passage explains that moving slowly and patiently is more effective for bird-watching than rushing. It highlights a trip to Okhla Bird Sanctuary where a slow approach led to better sightings.
